Hypothesis: H1: Marketplace order growth is accompanied by review score decline over time
Proposed Test: Monthly Mann-Kendall trend test, time-series decomposition
Risk: Confounding by seasonal holiday spikes or changing category mix

Hypothesis: H2: Customer dissatisfaction drops non-linearly with delay severity (exponential drop >7d)
Proposed Test: Kruskal-Wallis across delay buckets, piecewise threshold regression
Evidence Needed: Significant drop in review score / surge in 1-star % between buckets
Risk: Survivor bias on unfulfilled orders (not in delivered status)

Hypothesis: H3: Estimated delivery dates are systematically conservative, creating expectation buffers
Proposed Test: Skewness test and sign-test on delay_days (delivered - estimated)
Evidence Needed: Distribution significantly skewed left of zero (majority delivered early)
Risk: Conflating platform buffers with carrier SLA promises

Hypothesis: H4: Inter-regional corridors (e.g. SE to N/NE) suffer higher severe delay rates
Proposed Test: Chi-square test of independence on corridor delay proportions
Evidence Needed: Odds ratio of severe delay significantly higher for long-haul routes
Risk: Small sample sizes on sparse routes causing noise (need N >= 30 filter)

Hypothesis: H5: High freight cost does not guarantee superior delivery speed or satisfaction
Proposed Test: Partial correlation and quadrant efficiency analysis (cost vs speed)
Evidence Needed: Weak or zero correlation between freight ratio and delivery duration
Risk: Distance and product weight act as major confounders

Hypothesis: H6: Bulky categories have higher delay tolerance than express/small goods
Proposed Test: Interaction term (Category x Delay) in regression model
Evidence Needed: Slope of review drop vs delay is flatter for bulky goods
Risk: Subjective categorization of bulky vs non-bulky

Hypothesis: H7: Severe delivery delay is the primary independent driver of review score <= 2
Required Data: review_score, delay buckets, freight_ratio, order_value, categories, regions
Proposed Test: Multivariate Logistic Regression, Wald test, Odds Ratios
Evidence Needed: Severe delay Odds Ratio is highest and statistically significant (p < 0.001)
Risk: Multicollinearity between duration and delay; unobserved product quality defects

Hypothesis: H8: <15% of operational segments account for >35% of platform low reviews
Proposed Test: Lorenz curve, Gini coefficient, Pareto cumulative concentration curve
Evidence Needed: Top segments account for disproportionate share of low reviews
Risk: Over-segmentation creating artificially small, non-actionable clusters
